sources.quote: about 41 percent of those employers with fewer than five staff
sources.publisher: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
sources.title: Educational services - 61 - Businesses - Canadian Industry Statistics - Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
sources.evidence: In 2025, for employer establishments in the educational services industry, 41.3% of them were considered micro, employing less than five employees; small establishments accounted for 51.6%; and medium-sized establishments accounted for an additional 4% of the total number of establishments. Source: Statistics Canada, special tabulation, unpublished data, unclassified excluded, 2025.

sources.quote: corporate penalties under the civil deceptive marketing provisions can reach the greater of $10 million and 3 percent of annual worldwide gross revenues
sources.title: False or misleading representations
sources.evidence: For corporations, the penalty for a first-time violation is up to the greater of: $10 million ($15 million for each subsequent violation); and three times the value of the benefit derived from the deceptive conduct, or, if that amount cannot be reasonably determined, 3% of the corporation's annual worldwide gross revenue.

sources.quote: Discount claims must also clear the ordinary selling price rules
sources.title: Ordinary selling price - Competition Bureau Canada
sources.evidence: It is illegal to advertise fake discounts by promoting a made-up regular price, which violates the Competition Act. To prove that a regular price is valid, it must meet one of two legal tests: the volume test (more than 50% of sales of the product were at that price or higher within a reasonable period before or after the promotion) or the time test (the product was offered for sale, in good faith, at that price or higher for a substantial period of time immediately before or after the promotion).

sources.quote: Sections 248 and 249 of Quebec's Consumer Protection Act prohibit commercial advertising directed at children under 13
sources.publisher: Office de la protection du consommateur (Québec)
sources.title: Advertising Directed at Children
sources.evidence: The Consumer Protection Act prohibits commercial advertising that targets children under the age of thirteen. The Office de la protection du consommateur oversees compliance with this prohibition. There is a guide to the application of Sections 248 and 249 of the Consumer Protection Act addressing advertising directed at children under 13 years of age. To determine whether advertising is directed at children, the Act stipulates that it is necessary to take into account the context of the advertisement's presentation and the impression it gives.

sources.quote: Ontario's College of Teachers publishes a Find a Teacher register any parent can search to confirm an Ontario Certified Teacher's status and qualifications
sources.title: What information is displayed on the public register (Find a Teacher)? – Ontario College of Teachers
sources.evidence: Find a Teacher, the College's public register includes: members' names, teaching qualifications, terms, limitations and conditions, date of initial certification, College membership status, Sexual Abuse Prevention Program status, and disciplinary history, if applicable. The purpose of the public register is to identify whether someone is an Ontario Certified Teacher and their teaching qualifications, and provide information on a member's certificate status.

sources.quote: private secondary schools may issue credits toward the Ontario Secondary School Diploma only after ministry inspection
sources.title: Private schools | Government of Ontario
sources.evidence: Not all private schools can grant students the Ontario Secondary School Diploma (OSSD), or credits toward the OSSD. The Ministry inspects all private high schools seeking (or approved) to grant course credits towards the OSSD. If a school receives a satisfactory inspection report, the principal is authorized to grant credits towards OSSD. A private school must list on their website if they can grant credits toward the OSSD.

sources.title: OSSLT

Spring Administration starts Tuesday, March 30, 2027 and ends Monday, April 19, 2027. Grade 9 Assessment of Mathematics starts Tuesday, January 12, 2027 and ends Friday, February 5, 2027.

sources.title: Diploma exams – Overview | Alberta.ca
sources.evidence: To ensure students and teachers can concentrate on learning after lost instructional time due to labour action, Alberta's government has cancelled the January 2026 diploma examinations and Grade 9 Provincial Achievement Tests (PATs). Students will be automatically exempted from writing assessments in January; if they choose, a student may write their January diploma exam in April or June 2026.

sources.quote: those exams count for half the final grade
sources.title: Final results in Secondary IV and V | Gouvernement du Québec
sources.evidence: The moderated school mark and the ministerial examinations in Secondary IV and V each count for 50% of the final result for the competency or competencies evaluated. If the student's result on the ministerial examination is higher than the moderated school mark, only the mark on the examination will be taken into account. The ministerial examinations are administered every year in January, June and August.

sources.quote: 20 percent of eligible fees to a maximum of $500 per child, about $100 back, for qualifying programs of at least eight consecutive weeks
sources.title: Tax Credit for Children's Activities | Revenu Québec
sources.evidence: The tax credit is equal to 20% of the eligible registration or membership fees. You can claim a maximum of $500 in fees per child, for a maximum tax credit of $100 per child. The activities must be part of a program that takes place over at least eight consecutive weeks or at least five consecutive days (in the case of a summer camp), or a membership for a minimum period of eight consecutive weeks.
